Description:
Role: Senior AI Impact & Applied Innovation Specialist
Location: Cambridge UK
Salary: Competitive + Excellent Benefits

Are you ready to translate AstraZeneca's frontier AI capabilities into concrete impact for the organisation? The Applied AI Research team, part of the AI Science Innovation (AISI) group within Enterprise AI (EAI), sits at the intersection of frontier AI research and oncology R&D, with a mission to ensure that advances in foundation models, agentic systems, and biological AI find their way to the problems where they will have the greatest impact on how we discover and develop medicines.

As Senior AI Impact & Applied Innovation Specialist , Applied AI Research, you will be involved in both sides of that translation: identifying where frontier AI can address fundamental drug discovery questions for AstraZeneca, and orchestrating focused cross-departmental projects to answer them. You will maintain a structured view of AZ's highest-value AI science problems – mapping which questions most need answers, which frameworks are now mature enough to address them, and where AZ's unique data, biology, and portfolio create irreplaceable scientific advantage. You will also act as the scientific lead and orchestrator for delivering against those problems, assembling the right combination of expertise and resources and holding the scientific hypothesis through to a result that changes a decision.

This is a role for someone familiar with key questions across the drug discovery pipeline, who can attend a frontier AI seminar and immediately see which ideas are applicable to areas from target identification to trial design, and who has the scientific conviction to advocate for a particular problem in the face of competing priorities.

If you thrive at the intersection of machine learning and translational oncology and want to leave a direct mark on the scientific questions that shape AstraZeneca's pipeline, this role is for you.

Typical Accountabilities

AI Landscape & Opportunity Mapping:

- Maintain an interactive framework providing a structured, dynamic inventory of AZ's internal and external AI capabilities, including frontier models and platforms.

- Identify high-priority scientific questions—such as those in target discovery, combination therapy, tumor mapping, and trial design—where frontier AI can deliver significant value. Distinguish opportunities unique to AstraZeneca from those addressable with generic tools or public data.

Scientific Evaluation Standards:

- Apply scientific expertise and evaluation standards to AI-driven frameworks designed to maintain a live, structured record of R&D goals and decision-making.

- Design and apply evaluation approaches for generative and agentic systems, including harnesses, benchmarks, trajectory-level metrics and validated LLM-as-judge methods, and run structured red-teaming (adversarial testing, failure-mode taxonomies, pre-release and continuous monitoring).

- Advise on and test where AI agents can responsibly automate steps in scientific, clinical and operational research processes, defining oversight points, acceptance criteria and comparison with the manual baseline.

Forward-Deployed Embedding & Delivery:

- Translate scientific hypotheses into well-specified, time-bounded projects with pre-defined success criteria, with a clear path to integration and deployment; orchestrate the delivery of these projects

- Establish frameworks for quantifying impacts of AI projects and measuring impact for the business and implement these for active cross-functional projects.

Stakeholder Communication & Leadership:

- Communicate AI science priorities, programmed status, and strategic recommendations to senior stakeholders across EAI, Oncology R&D and Biopharma R&D; act as the scientific bridge between AISI strategy and execution-layer teams, ensuring that frontier insight translates into actionable work and that delivery blockers are visible to leadership.

Essential Requirements:

- Advanced degree (PhD preferred; Master's with substantial relevant experience considered) in a quantitative biological or computational discipline: computational biology, bioinformatics, machine learning, statistics, or a closely related field.

- Demonstrated experience applying AI/ML methods to clinical, genomic, transcriptomic, or other biomedical data in a drug development or translational research context.

- Strong scientific literacy across the oncology drug development pipeline, from target identification and preclinical biology through biomarker development, clinical trial design, and Phase 1/2 decision-making.

- Familiarity with the current landscape of AI in drug development, including foundation models for biological and clinical data, perturbation prediction, digital pathology, and agentic research systems.

- Demonstrated ability to frame rigorous scientific or clinical questions and translate them into tractable AI problems with well-specified success criteria.

- Experience evaluating the quality of AI models in a scientific or clinical context, including understanding of validation standards, confounding, shortcut learning, and the distinction between prognostic and predictive signals.

- Track record of working effectively across multidisciplinary teams, including both technical AI/ML specialists and experimental or clinical scientists.
- Excellent written and oral scientific communication, including the ability to present technical material to non-technical senior audiences and to distil complex landscapes into actionable recommendations.
- Comfort with ambiguity and a bias for action; able to make well-reasoned prioritization decisions under uncertainty and to advocate for them.

Desirable Requirements:

- Direct experience with generative AI and agentic systems applied to life sciences, particularly for clinical insights.
- Direct experience with multimodal foundation models, particularly for computational pathology, for response prediction, subtyping and other common research tasks.

- Direct experience with multimodal data integration, for example combining clinical, genomic, transcriptomic, imaging, and/or pathology data.

- Familiarity with CRISPR functional genomics, perturbation prediction, or virtual cell approaches and their application to target discovery or combination prioritization.

- Familiarity with AI benchmarking methodologies and the challenges of evaluating foundation models on clinically meaningful tasks.

- Experience with AI prioritization or portfolio management methodologies – including problem identification, value assessment, and structured decision frameworks.
- A record of scientific contribution (e.g., peer-reviewed publications), ideally including AI/ML or clinical AI venues, that establishes credibility with technical, clinical, and scientific audiences

ABOUT FRACTILE

Fractile was founded in 2022 on the bet that, eventually, the world’s most capable AI systems would be limited in their impact by the time taken to produce useful outputs. We bet everything on the logical conclusion: that the only way to truly unlock this latent value, to make speed viable at scale, was to radically re-invent the hardware that we run our frontier AI models on. Ever since, we have been building chips and systems that tackle this problem: how to efficiently generate output at thousands of tokens per second, while handling the complexity and capacity challenges of operating large models at very long contexts.

The workloads that push to the limits of the current frontier are already transformational; it is the technical and economic limits on inference speed that are constraining progress. The defining work of the 21st century will be marked by the engine of inference delivering immense and diffuse chains of intellectual inquiry, in drug discovery, in software engineering, in materials discovery, in any field where progress is driven by deep reasoning and intelligence to resolve complex problems.

Fractile isn't another AI startup gluing together frameworks. We are designing a full-stack execution engine: hardware, compiler, runtime, to build the world's largest language models 100 x faster than today's systems. That ambition forces us to rethink everything from first principles.

For compiler engineers, this is a rare moment: the architecture is still being shaped. The IR, the lowering strategy, the optimisation passes, the execution model - you get to define its future.

YOU MAY ALSO HAVE:

Title: Lead Data Scientist
Description:
Lead Data Scientist, Obsero
UK, remote, full time. £80,000 to £100,000 plus equity.
Find out why AI recommends one brand over another. Turn our AI search data into the GEO playbook, the recommendation engine and the models that tell customers what to do next.
About Obsero
Obsero is one of the UK's leading AI search startups. We track how brands are cited and recommended across ChatGPT, Gemini, Perplexity, Google AI Mode and Claude, so marketing teams can see where they stand in AI answers and what to do about it.
The problem
Every day our platform runs thousands of prompts across the major AI platforms and records what comes back: which brands get mentioned, which sources get cited, how they are described and how that changes over time. It is now one of the richest datasets on AI search anywhere. Today the platform tells customers where they stand. The question every marketer actually wants answered is why an LLM recommends one brand over another, and what they should do about it. Your job is to answer it, and to take the platform from insight to action.
Why join now

- We've just raised $1.2m, led by SFC Capital, to build specialist AI agents trained on the GEO playbook from a year of client work
- In our first year we captured and analysed over 10 million AI answers, and that number is growing fast
- You'll be the first data scientist, so you'll set how we turn that data into insight
- Meaningful equity, alongside a salary of £80,000 to £100,000
The role
This is a lead role reporting to a founder. You will own the problem end to end, from a clean, trusted dataset through to models running in the product. Our lead data engineer owns how the data is captured, cleaned and stored, so your time goes on what it means rather than on fixing it.
What you'll own

- The GEO playbook: using our historic prompt data to understand what drives LLMs to recommend one brand over another, separating the factors that genuinely move visibility from the ones that only look like they do
- The recommendation engine: productising Obsero's GEO recommendation engine in the platform, and measuring whether recommendations work so results feed back into the engine
- Predictive models: predicting the likely impact of different actions for each customer, so they know what to do first
- New insight: exploring new ways to analyse the data, prototyping quickly and turning the best ideas into features
This is not a reporting or dashboarding role. We want someone who asks better questions of the data than we do, and builds the models and products that answer them.
What you'll need

- Several years of hands-on data science, with a track record of taking models from analysis into production
- Strong Python and SQL, comfortable building the analysis and feature pipelines your models need
- Statistical modelling, causal inference or experimentation, and the judgement to tell correlation from cause in messy, real-world data
- Experience with recommendation systems, ranking or predictive modelling
- Hands-on with LLMs and NLP, and properly curious about how AI platforms decide what to recommend
- The ability to explain complex findings clearly to marketers, consultants and founders
- Product-minded, focused on what will change a customer's results
- Comfortable owning a problem end to end in a small team
Nice to have

- An understanding of SEO or GEO
You'll need to be based in the UK with the right to work here.
What success looks like

- A GEO playbook grounded in evidence that our consultants and customers use
- A recommendation engine live in the platform, with customers acting on what it tells them
- Measurable improvement in customer visibility from the actions it prioritises
- Insight that sets Obsero apart from every other AI search tool
How we hire
Intro call with the Chief Product Officer, a technical conversation with our lead engineer, a presentation and then meeting the CEO.
How to apply
Apply through the link on this ad. Tell us briefly about a model you took from idea to production, and what difference it made.
